name: pattern-language
note: The pattern-language index. Each pattern is an algal manifest — a constructive diagram resolving a small, declared system of forces. Links point to larger patterns the pattern helps complete and smaller patterns it contains, as in A Pattern Language. The index is data; the diagrams are runnable.

patterns.name: bounded-slice
patterns.context: reading evidence from an artifact too large for the window

patterns.name: provenance-line
patterns.context: an emitted report whose reader must judge how much to trust it
forces: the header competes with the body
silent clipping is worse than no extract

patterns.name: declared-failure-path
patterns.context: a step whose result can fail to fit its invariant
forces: the run must not die silently

patterns.name: context-view
patterns.context: a judgment cell working inside a decomposed subsystem
forces: the judge needs the subsystem's evidence
outside forces must not leak in
what was seen must be replayable

patterns.name: piecemeal-tradition
patterns.context: a working form challenged by a candidate variant
forces: the form must improve over generations
what runs is never rewritten in place

patterns.name: verdict-first
patterns.context: an emitted report whose reader must learn the verdict instantly
forces: color carries meaning a pipe loses
the smallest diagram is still a diagram

programs.name: correlate
programs.does: ensemble -> signed interaction graph (pair-probe decide cell per pair)

programs.name: decompose
programs.does: interaction graph -> k nearly-independent subsystems (bounded repeat of decompose-step merges)

programs.name: diagram
programs.does: subsystem -> spawned constructive diagram (child digest = the pattern's content address)

programs.name: synthesize
programs.does: the whole method as one digest-wired organism: enumerate -> correlate -> decompose -> each(diagram) -> realize

programs.name: pair-probe
programs.does: one misfit pair -> interact/sign judgment; embedded in correlate by digest

programs.name: decompose-step
programs.does: one agglomerative merge round in pure expr; embedded in decompose's repeat by digest

ensembles.name: cli-report
ensembles.does: 8 misfits for a terminal report (visual design)

ensembles.name: village
ensembles.does: Alexander's Appendix I worked example: 141 Indian-village misfits + his published unsigned interaction table (1434 normalized links)

ensembles.name: algal-src
ensembles.does: transfer test: the algal runtime's own src/ — 48 modules as misfit obligations, import edges as links, AGENTS.md subsystem tour as oracle

habitats.name: status-line
habitats.does: 4 verdict-line variants compete on 6 labeled cases (train/validation/holdout) under an expr scorer; report verifies offline
